property_summary: For any caller and any new owner, after transferring ownership the stored owner() equals the transferred address regardless of who queries it; the mutant instead returns msg.sender, so it returns the querying caller rather than the set owner whenever they differ.
p_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,address,address): Ownable: caller is not the owner
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,address,address): owner() must return the transferred owner regardless of caller

property_summary: Ownership can never become the zero address via transferOwnership: for any fuzzed newOwner the reference contract either reverts or leaves a nonzero owner(), while the mutant accepts address(0) and c.owner() becomes zero.

For any non-zero address, the owner's call to transferOwnership(newOwner) must succeed (only the zero address is forbidden); the mutant additionally forbids transferring to the current owner, so it reverts when newOwner equals the owner.

After initialize and updateAlloSettings, for any nonzero address passed by the owner, updateRoundImplementation stores it and c.roundImplementation() always equals that address; the mutant accepts zero addresses too, so for a zero input P reverts while M stores address(0).

After any successful updateRoundImplementation call, c.roundImplementation() must be nonzero (P reverts on the zero address so it never stores 0); the mutant, having dropped the require, stores address(0) and violates this for a zero-address input.

For any caller, updateRoundImplementation only changes roundImplementation when the caller is the contract owner; the buggy inverse modifier lets any non-owner change it and blocks the owner, so asserting the post-call value equals the requested implementation (with actor=owner) distinguishes P from M.
